findings.title: Stable Channel Update for Desktop
findings.summary_md: Google promoted Chrome 157 to the stable channel on November 3, 2026 for Windows, Mac and Linux, rolling out over the coming days and weeks. The update ships 213 security fixes, including seven critical flaws: CVE-2026-121156 (buffer overflow in Dawn, $10,000 bounty, reported by Zhenpeng (Leo) Lin at depthfirst on September 30), CVE-2026-121229 (memory corruption in ANGLE, $1,000, reported by @mfx on September 17), plus five more criticals with no listed bounty reported by Google, Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, and Wenbin Liu. Google paid $31,000 across the release and left bounties undecided for 39 flaws, and states the update contains no in-the-wild exploitation. Desktop builds are 157.0.8103.38 on Linux and 157.0.8103.38 or .39 on Windows and Mac, with Chrome for Android at 157.0.8103.38.

findings.title: Chrome 157: Stable Released with 213 Security Fixes and 7 Critical Flaws
findings.summary_md: Early coverage of Google's November 3, 2026 Chrome Releases blog post, noting Chrome 157 at 157.0.8103.38 or .39 on Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.38 on Linux with 213 security fixes including seven critical and 77 high severity, rolling out over days to weeks. Walks through manual update steps via About Google Chrome and relaunch, and notes what remains unconfirmed from the vendor announcement. Published November 4, 2026 at 11:07 JST.

findings.title: Chrome 157 Is Out: 213 Security Fixes and What Is New
findings.summary_md: Early coverage noting Google promoted Chrome 157 to stable on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 for Windows, Mac and Linux, with Android builds heading to Google Play. Counts the 213 fixes as seven critical, 77 high, 75 medium and 54 low, and states Google's post does not report in-the-wild exploitation. Also highlights HTML-in-Canvas reaching stable and enterprise release notes about security updates reaching new browser processes without a restart.
